keyFindings.description: The body's Threads ledger reads '6 resolved, 0 unresolved' and lists six node ids. GitHub answers nine, all resolved: gh api graphql reviewThreads(first:100){totalCount} returns 9. The three missing are round three's - PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6vlLh9 (the INFRA-117 supersede note), PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6vlLiJ (version.go's contract-19 entry) and PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6vlLiN (the headline wait test) - all fixed in 13dc9d4d9d6185646beb3aed5225665bc8d13a88 and answered by me before the body's newest bullet was written, so the body was edited after them and left them out. skills/legion-worker/references/pr-body.md makes ## Verification the ledger the reviewer and the merger check against GitHub, and a body line that no longer matches the facts a finding against the implementer rather than a line a later role rewrites. This is the issue's own class in the issue's own body: a count typed into a record a later role trusts, which the forge contradicts. Set it to nine and add the three bullets in the existing shape.

The new guard gives false assurance about the class it names, and it does not scan the root where this pull request deleted the same instruction. I ran its three regexes rather than reading them: they catch the paragraph that regressed and the template's **CI:** field line, and they miss 'That reference is the sole definition of the CI line' - the sentence this branch deletes from packages/daemon/internal/prompts/roles/implementer.md:12, because defines? does not match definition - and they miss 'The body's CI line is the runs GitHub started for the code head', which is exactly the 'subject of a verb that says what it contains' slot the comment at :156-166 claims is covered, and 'populate the CI line' and 'Keep the body's CI line current'. So the seventeen-line grammar essay specifies a rule the code does not hold, and a later reader who trusts it will believe the class is closed. Separately the scan is files(staged) alone (:185) while its sibling guard one screen up uses [staged, promptsRoot] (:139-140) and promptsRoot is already bound at :24; prompts are forward-merged from main with the same 'a merge keeps both sides by design' hazard the comment itself describes, so the identical regression can re-land in a role prompt with no conflict and no red test. Two remedies, either acceptable: widen the scan to both roots and make the rule match what the comment claims, or keep the rule and cut the comment to what it does - it pins these shapes, it is not a closed class. A flat ban on the phrase is also open: my own sweep of skills/, packages/claude-envoy/legion/ and packages/daemon/internal/prompts/ for the phrase in any of its spellings returns zero hits today, so a flat ban has no false positive to answer for in either root. The choice is the implementer's; the false claim is not.

The 300-file caveat this branch adds cannot be acted on with the command it follows. The reviewer is told to run gh api .../compare/<ci head>...<headRefOid> --jq '[.files[].filename] | all(startswith(".legion/"))', which collapses the list to one boolean, and then told that a true from a compare of 300 files decides nothing and must not be approved on. The reviewer cannot see the count, so the rule is unenforceable as written and the reviewer it binds reads true and approves - the outcome the sentence forbids. I am the bound party and met it this round: my own invocation printed the count only because I added one. Emit it from the same call, for instance --jq '[.files]|length' beside the boolean, and say that 300 means undecided. READY's own equivalent cap has a refusal for this (READY_FILES_TRUNCATED); the reviewer's read has none.

roundThreeFindingVerified: Fixed in 7aaf2e9ac1a9b08e74df20552818fd3621080341. The paragraph defining the CI line is deleted from skills/legion-worker/references/pr-body.md and from the generated packages/claude-envoy copy, which is a rebuild rather than a hand edit; the CHANGELOG blank line is restored. My own sweep of skills/, packages/claude-envoy/legion/, packages/daemon/internal/prompts/ and packages/pi-legion/scripts/ for the phrase in any spelling now returns zero hits. The guard added with the fix is the subject of a finding of its own above; the deletion itself is clean.
